$comment: TF-C51 (D-FF1-STATICLIB-FAT-ARCHIVE): the FAT/merged static-library RUNTIME witness at the corpus tier. Building a `-staticlib` while passing INPUT `--resolve-library` static archives MERGES their members into the output library. This example needs a NESTED dependsOn (D-EXAMPLES-RUNNER-MULTI-ARTIFACT extension): each target's dependsOn is the FAT lib `fatlib.a` (from fatlib.c, defining dss_fat_extra), whose OWN nested dependsOn is the INPUT lib `input.a` (from input.c, defining dss_input_answer==42). The runner builds bottom-up: input.a, then fatlib.a RESOLVING input.a (the FAT MERGE -> fatlib.a carries BOTH members), then main RESOLVING ONLY fatlib.a. main references dss_input_answer, reaching it SOLELY via the merged copy in fatlib.a (input.a is NOT on main's --resolve-library) -> runs -> exit 42 IFF the merge worked. RED-ON-DISABLE (both gates verified, x86_64 native + arm64 qemu): (1) BUILD -- removing the merge restores the D_StaticLibFatArchiveUnsupported fail-loud so fatlib.a's dependsOn build returns rc!=0 -> red; (2) RUN -- a silent-no-op merge leaves fatlib.a without dss_input_answer and main STILL links (the open D-LINK-EXEC-UNDEFINED-SYMBOL-FAIL-LOUD gap: DSS emits the exec with the symbol unresolved) but fails at RUNTIME with the loader's 'undefined symbol: dss_input_answer' -> exit 127 != 42 -> the runner's exit-code assert fires -> red. NOTE: artifact names track the driver's `<sourceStem>.a`/`.lib`/`.exe` output naming (input.c -> input.a|input.lib, fatlib.c -> fatlib.a|fatlib.lib, main.c -> main|main.exe), NOT a 'lib' prefix. x86_64 runs natively under WSL / the ubuntu leg; arm64 under qemu-aarch64; pe64 (COFF .lib -> .exe) natively on the Windows leg (verified: fatlib.lib merges input.lib -> main.exe exit 42); macho64 arm64 NATIVELY on the darwin leg, build-clean + SkippedCrossHost elsewhere. D-TEST-EXAMPLES-DEPENDSON-UNCOVERED-ON-DARWIN: the macho64 arm is what makes the NESTED dependsOn path RUN on darwin at all. Before it, NEITHER dependsOn manifest carried a `darwin` runOn, so integrated_tests' `buildDependsOnArtifactCli` -- which SKIPS an example outright when no target's runOn matches the host -- was reached by ZERO checks on the leg this project gates on every cycle, leaving the recursion free to rot behind a green suite. MEASURED on darwin arm64, the full bottom-up chain: input.a (426 B), then fatlib.a RESOLVING it -> 774 B (the merge -- it carries BOTH members), then main RESOLVING ONLY fatlib.a, spawned -> exit 42. RUN-gate RED-ON-DISABLE re-MEASURED on this host, not merely inherited from the linux/windows legs: build fatlib.a WITHOUT the nested resolve and it stays 420 B (unmerged); main still links, but dyld aborts with `Symbol not found: _dss_input_answer` -> exit 134 != 42 -> red. Note the darwin RUN-gate signal is SIGABRT-134 from dyld, not the 127 the ELF loader gives; either way it is != 42, which is all the exit-code assert needs. D-EXAMPLES-DEPENDSON-NO-RELEASE-OPTIMIZER-ARM (the `release` arm below): this manifest and staticlib_resolve_roundtrip's are the corpus's ONLY two that use the runner's per-target `dependsOn` key, and until now NEITHER declared an `optimizedPipelines` arm -- so the whole `dependsOn` / `-staticlib` / `--resolve-library` static-link path, INCLUDING the fat merge, had only ever been compiled through the baseline pipeline, which is a bare `Identity`, i.e. a no-op. WHAT THE ARM IS FOR: with the runner building each prerequisite library under the arm's OWN configuration, the `release` arm compiles the WHOLE bottom-up chain through the shipped release pipeline -- input.a, then the merging fatlib.a build, then main -- so the members that cross the merge and land in the exec are release-pipeline output instead of baseline output. That is the first time the shipped optimizer reaches the staticlib and fat-merge MIR shapes on any leg, which is what lets a future optimizer regression over them RED here instead of passing green. WHY THE ARM CAN ATTRIBUTE ITS DIFFERENCE TO THE ARCHIVE: `main.c` is deliberately thin -- one extern declaration and one call, no locals, no arithmetic, no inlinable callee -- so it offers the pipeline nothing of its own. `dss_input_answer` (input.c) is the member `main` references and therefore the one whose code reaches the exec, so it carries the arm's witness: an inlinable helper, a loop-invariant addend and locals for Mem2Reg to promote, still returning exactly 42. `dss_fat_extra` (fatlib.c) is shaped the same way and still returns 7, so the fat lib's OWN member is optimizer input too rather than only the merged one. `mustDifferFromBaseline: true` is therefore aimed AT THE PREREQUISITE BUILDS: if the runner stops threading the arm's configuration into them, or if someone simplifies either library function back to a single `return`, the expectation is that the optimized exec has nothing left to differ by and the arm REDS instead of quietly asserting x == x. That expectation is INFERRED, not measured here -- but it rests on a DSS measurement of exactly this shape, recorded under D-TEST-CORPUS-77-OPTIMIZED-ARMS-WITNESS-NOTHING: a consumer whose only call was external produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL pe64 image under `debug` and `release`, and only giving the consumer an inlinable helper, an accumulator and a loop made the two configs diverge. WHAT THE PER-DEPENDENCY OPT-IN ADDS OVER THE ARM-LEVEL ONE, now that every `dependsOn` entry above -- INCLUDING THE NESTED `input` ONE -- also carries `mustDifferFromBaseline: true`: the ARM-LEVEL key compares the EXECUTABLE's bytes, and an exec can differ between the two configs for reasons entirely its own -- main.c's translation unit, image layout, anything the pipeline touches on the consumer side -- so a green arm-level assertion is still consistent with BOTH archives having been built at BASELINE the whole time. Only the PER-DEPENDENCY key compares EACH PREREQUISITE'S OWN IMAGE, arm vs baseline, so it is the only form here that actually asserts `fatlib.c` and `input.c` were compiled through the arm's pipeline. And because the key is honoured at every nesting depth, arming the NESTED entry is what puts the BOTTOM of the bottom-up chain -- the archive whose member later crosses the merge -- under the assertion DIRECTLY, instead of leaving it inferred from the top of the chain. The key is opt-in (absent means report-only). NO corpus dependency declared it before this manifest and staticlib_resolve_roundtrip's, so it shipped exercised only by the two runners' planted fixtures -- these are the first corpus dependencies to arm it. SAFE TO ARM, MEASURED (shipped CLI, Windows host, cross-compiling each source to each `-staticlib` and comparing debug vs release BYTE-wise, not by size): input.c pe64-x86_64 886 -> 674, elf64-x86_64 1684 -> 1468, elf64-aarch64 1524 -> 1380, macho64-arm64 780 -> 656; fatlib.c 866 -> 662, 1672 -> 1464, 1512 -> 1376, 768 -> 648 in the same order -- all eight DIFFER, so no armed entry is a guaranteed red. That is an image measurement, NOT a leg result. Do not re-quote those byte counts as a pin: a COFF archive embeds the source stem, so the pe64 figures move if a file is renamed; what is asserted is the DIFFERENCE, never the size. D-LINK-NONEXTERNAL-DEFINED-SYMBOL-READ-AS-BLOCK-LABEL-NOT-ATOM -- WHY `dss_input_add` AND `dss_fat_bump` ARE `static`, RESTORED 2026-08-20 (cycle P22) IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THE READER FIX THEY WITNESS. The keyword IS the test. A file-local function called from an exported one, inside an archive member, is the shape the COFF and Mach-O archive-member readers used to demote to a bodyless interior block label; with the keyword this chain used to red EARLIER than staticlib_resolve_roundtrip's -- not at the exec link but at the FAT-MERGE staticlib build itself, with `error[K_SymbolUndefined] ... relocation in symbol #N references undefined symbol #M (not declared by any AssembledFunction, ExternImport, nor AssembledData item)` on pe64-x86_64 and macho64-arm64 while both elf64 legs built and linked fine. Without the keyword both helpers are ordinary externals, which every reader has always promoted to atoms, and this example would run 42 while asserting nothing about them. ★★ WHAT THE TWO COPIES ASSERT THAT ONE COULD NOT: `input.c`'s local CROSSES THE MERGE and so must survive TWO read-backs -- the fat `-staticlib` build reading `input.a` to merge the member, then the exec link reading `fatlib.a` to pull it -- while `fatlib.c`'s local belongs to the fat library's OWN member, which `main` never references, so it must survive being written into the merged archive beside the merged one and then correctly left alone. MEASURED 2026-08-20 with `nm` on the intermediates (elf64-x86_64, baseline): `input.a` carries its local as `sym_84`, the merged `fatlib.a` carries BOTH members with the merged copy RENUMBERED to `sym_2` and fatlib's own still `sym_84`, and the linked executable contains `dss_input_answer` plus the merged local only. The whole three-step chain returns rc=0 on pe64-x86_64, elf64-x86_64, elf64-aarch64, macho64-arm64 AND macho64-x86_64, and the pe64 executable runs exit 42 at both configurations. ⚠⚠ THE WITNESS IS THE BASELINE ARM AND THE `release` ARM CANNOT REACH THIS DEFECT: MEASURED with `nm`, at `--config=release` the local symbol is absent from the archive entirely, because Inlining removes the call and DCE removes the function, so no file-local relocation survives for a reader to get wrong. A release-only test of it is vacuous. `examples/c/staticlib_file_local_atoms` is the example built to hold at BOTH configurations, and it is where the silent (unreferenced) arm and the file-local DATA half are covered. Leg-by-leg results are NOT recorded here -- whoever runs the legs writes them.
